title: Container artifact lifecycle indexing and driver compatibility workflow
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We need a reliable, auditable workflow for indexing container artifacts, attaching canonical SBOMs and immutably pinning CUDA/driver compatibility metadata across LTS channels. Current gaps: disparate SBOM formats in registry, ad-hoc driver pin annotations, and no automated gate that prevents rollout when driver/CUDA matrix mismatches occur. Goal: implement an index+catalog service and a release playbook that enforces compatibility checks and rollout gates for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
tasks: Design registry index schema: canonical image identifier, build-id, sbom-checksum (sha256), driver_pinset (gpu_family -> driver_version), cuda_compat_table reference
Implement SBOM ingestion pipeline: accept SPDX and CycloneDX, normalize to canonical JSON and compute sbom-checksum
Add immutability layer to image tags used by LTS channels (lts/YYYY.MM or channel:lts-YYYY-MM) and write retention rules
Create automated compatibility validator that rejects images whose driver_pinset lacks supported entries for target hardware (NVIDIA T4/A100/V100)
Integrate vulnerability scanning step that fails gate if critical CVEs exceed threshold for LTS channel
Wire index to Console: expose per-image driver matrix, SBOM link, and tokenized provenance for customer-facing audit
Create playbook for rolling driver updates with canary cohorts and automatic rollback on latency/correctness regressions
Add CI job to rebuild affected images when base CUDA or distro CVEs are patched and create PRs for bumping pinsets
acceptance_criteria: Index service stores canonical metadata for all new images pushed to registry and exposes an API to query sbom-checksum and driver_pinset
SBOM normalization accepts SPDX and CycloneDX inputs and produces a single canonical artifact with sha256 checksum
Compatibility validator runs as a pre-deploy gate and blocks rollout when no compatible driver is found for a declared LTS channel
Release Console shows driver compatibility matrix and an action button to mark an image as LTS-stable
Automated CVE threshold check integrated into gate (configurable per channel) and documented in playbook
At least one canary rollout executed for runtime-1.19 demonstrating rollback triggered by a synthetic latency regression metric
decisions: Use sbom-checksum (sha256) as the canonical binding between container image and its SBOM to avoid relying on tag names
Normalize SBOMs to SPDX v2.2 JSON internally; accept CycloneDX and translate during ingestion
Adopt a hybrid versioning scheme: semantic runtime version plus channel tags (example: runtime-1.19, lts-2025.04) to make LTS assignment explicit
Driver compatibility will be represented as a small matrix per image rather than a free-form string to simplify automated checks
Gating policy: fail fast on missing compatibility entries; allow warnings for non-critical mismatches with manual override recorded in audit log

rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Canary: Enable validator on 'staging' registry and run compatibility checks for nightly builds for 2 weeks
Phase 2 - Internal Beta: Add index metadata to all images for internal teams; enable automated CVE threshold checks for non-prod LTS channels
Phase 3 - Controlled Production: Enforce gates for Dedicated customers on new LTS images; run canary cohorts (1% -> 10% -> 50%) with 24h observation windows
Phase 4 - Full Enforcement: Block rollout to all clusters unless index and compatibility checks pass; provide documented override process requiring two approvers
risk_mitigation: Maintain a rollback image pinset for each LTS channel and keep it evergreen until new pinset validated
Fallback policy for private customers: if gate blocks and they opt-out, require signed attestation and run compatibility tests in-customer
Throttle enforcement during high traffic windows and provide telemetry for quick rollback triggers
Short-circuit: if SBOM conversion fails transiently, mark as warning and queue for manual triage to avoid blocking emergency CVE patches
notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on the indexing and gating workflow rather than full UI polish. Subsequent follow-ups will cover Console UX refinements and migration scripts for historical images.
